item.title: SQL Server Techniques for Accurate Business Day Calculation Between Dates
item.description:
“SQL Server Techniques for Accurate Business Day Calculation Between Dates”

How can one accurately determine the number of business days (weekdays, typically Monday through Friday) spanning a given start date and end date within SQL Server? Furthermore, what efficient methods exist for incorporating exclusion lists like public or company holidays into this calculation?

Various solutions have been proposed, ranging from concise mathematical formulas leveraging built-in date functions to iterative loops and custom user-defined functions (UDFs). Below are several distinct and accepted strategies for tackling this common requirement.

item.title: SQL Server: Extracting Date Part from Datetime Efficiently
item.description:
“SQL Server: Extracting Date Part from Datetime Efficiently”

When working with date and time data in SQL Server, it’s common to need only the date portion of a DATETIME or DATETIME2 value, discarding the time component. Several methods exist to achieve this, each with its own nuances in terms of performance, compatibility, and readability. This exploration delves into these techniques, providing practical examples and highlighting their advantages.

The Core Challenge: Isolating Date from Datetime

The fundamental issue is that SQL Server’s DATETIME data type inherently stores both date and time. To isolate the date, we need a way to either truncate the time or explicitly cast the value to a type that only holds dates.
